Greg “The Hammer” Valentine.t: This man has had many very memorable matches in JCW, including an infamous and very bloody “Dog Collar Chain” match versus The Rude Boy. He also took on his legendary nemesis Tito Santana in a steel cage on the Legends & Icons show at The Gathering, and even teamed with his old Dream Team partner Brutus “The Barber” Beefcake on a couple of occasions.

Hollywood Chuck Hogan.t: Hollywood Chuck Hogan is a JCW Hall of Famer and a strange abnormality in JCW. He wore a rubber Cryptkeeper mask and a baseball uniform. We suspect he called himself Hollywood Chuck Hogan because his hairline started in the back of his head like Hulk Hogan's. It was amazing to see how the Juggalos gravitated towards this character, showing him absolute love. Only in JCW!

Ian Rotten.t: You may or may not have heard of Ian Rotten, but just know this man is a piece of shit. However, we'd be lying if we denied him his JCW history. He was one half of a tag team called the Bloody Brothers, and they wrecked shop throughout JCW. He also teamed with his brother Axl on several occasions at Bloodymania, and he had his own singles matches. He was a rude, crude, bad ass and a real-life heel.

Kamala.t: Kamala “The Ugandan Headhunter” provided JCW fans with some extremely unforgettable moments over the years. His battle with 2 Tuff Tony at West Side Wars in Vegas was epic, and his battles against Jimmy “Superfly” Snuka were incredible. Most memorable, however, happened at the Gathering of the Juggalos when, after a match with Cowboy Bob Orton, somebody from the crowd passed Kamala a joint. After hitting the joint he suddenly could speak perfect English, stunning the crowd as he began to sing a song about the blues.

Kevin Thorn.t: Kevin Thorn, The Vampire, the modern Dracula type. Thorn performed in JCW for about a year during a stretch when the company was having pay-per-views out in Pontiac, Michigan twice a month. Always a professional and always a nice guy, it was a blessing to have Kevin Thorn around. A fantastic wrestler open to anything.

Kid Kash.t: Kid Kash first appeared in JCW when he wrestled under the name Kid Kock, tag-teaming with Feminem to go up against ICP in the main event of JCW Vol. 3. Since then, Kid Kash caused nothing but ruckus in JCW. It even spilled over into TNA's rings, where his battles with ICP continued.

Monty Brown.t: Former NFL player Monty Brown was an athletic specimen of perfection. Violent J and Shaggy have gone on record many times saying one of their favorite opponents ever was Monty Brown. He worked his ass off for everything he got — and he got a lot! His work was flawless. Wrestling him was a night off no matter what you had going on in that ring; he took total care of you. He was an absolute certified professional, one of the most talented men to ever step into a JCW ring, and that's a fact!

Rob Conway.t: Once known as The Mercenary (the original Mercenary before Shane Mercer), Rob Conway was always quick to take a payout to help or hurt anyone for money. He chose no sides, he only chose the money. Conway was a true JCW standout and former World Heavyweight Champion. A reliable, tough, serious worker — the kind of man that's an absolute role model in the dressing room. He's been a top guy in the company on many occasions and has had quite a few successful runs in JCW.

Sabu.t: Sabu's history in JCW is extremely extensive. He held the JCW World Championship on 2 occasions. Sabu appeared at over 10 Bloodymania events. Sabu was as JCW as JCW can be — not only wrestling all across the country and touring with ICP as well, but also wrestling in the company's private parties. Putting in work like that just for your friends shows what kind of man Sabu really was. We love Sabu. We miss him. ICP tribute him every single night by pointing to the sky at the beginning of their shows.

Steve Corino.t: Steve Corino was one of the best talkers in the game, a true professional in professional wrestling. He could be about to have a jobber match, get on the mic and sell it like it was about to be a main event that could sell out any building in America! He was that good, and he was a heel, which meant people wanted to kill him! It was an honor to have Steve Corino entertaining us over the years in JCW.

Terry Funk.t: From the Double Cross Ranch in Amarillo, Texas, Terry Funk is a former JCW World Heavyweight Champion. He became a staple of Bloodymania with many iconic matches at various Bloodymania events over the years. Funk teamed with ICP on several occasions, Sabu, and even had a 3-way vs Dusty Rhodes and The Rude Boy. It was always such an enormous pleasure to have a true hardcore icon like Terry Funk on any JCW card, anytime.

The Ring Ryders.t: To this very day, The Ring Ryders are considered the greatest tag team to ever grace a JCW ring. They are by far the most popular tag team to ever come along in JCW. They've held the JCW Tag Team Championship belts on four separate occasions. Ryder Red & Ryder Blue are true JCW future Hall of Famers — it's incredible that hasn't happened already.

The Thomaselli Brothers.t: One of the most hated, yet undeniably toughest tag teams to ever compete in JCW has to be the Thomaselli Bros. They were always damn near starting riots with the fans. Finally, after losing a “Loser Leaves Town” match, they would at last be gone. Or would they? They returned the very next month with new gear and face masks calling themselves “The Haters” — a very suitable name for these two brothers from Chicago.

The Weedman.t: Never has JCW seen a more innovative wrestler than The Weedman. Just by incorporating a few blunts into his matches, The Weedman did things in boots and spandex that Cheech & Chong could never have thought of. The Weedman often feuded with Officer Colt Cabana and teamed with 2 Tuff Tony on many occasions. Always a fan favorite, The Weedman is a true JCW icon and future Hall of Famer.

Tracy Smothers.t: Nobody in JCW's history has ever caused more chaos, panic and absolute infuriating anger than this man, Tracy Smothers. His constant belittling of Juggalos and waving his rebel flag truly showed that he was absolutely fearless in any Juggalo environment. For that, he was also respected and admired. That's why today he rests on top as a JCW Hall of Famer, one of the best to ever do it. God bless Tracy Smothers.

“Rowdy” Roddy Piper.t: Piper made several appearances in JCW over the years. He performed his infamous Piper's Pit segments, including a very memorable one with Scott D'Amore. He also wrestled on several occasions, but without a shadow of a doubt, we're most proud that “Rowdy” Roddy Piper — the legendary icon — wrestled his very last match at the Gathering of the Juggalos, where Piper and Cowboy Bob Orton took on Terry Funk and Mick Foley.

2 Tuff Tony.t:
2 Tuff Tony’s place in JCW history is etched in stone. The same crusty, bloodstained slab the company was built on, probably behind a Waffle House somewhere. A true-to-life JCW Day 1’nner, Tony was there when the ring was still half duct-tape and dreams.

As both a JCW and Louisville Pro Wrestling Hall of Famer, and a former 5-time JCW World Champion, plus tag team and American Champ, Tony’s legacy is that of a battle-scarred road warrior who earned every belt, every bruise, and every busted beer bottle to the dome. He’s the walking, brawling embodiment of that Juggalo spirit uncompromising, hard-hitting, and always down for a backyard rumble or a parking lot BBQ brawl.

A day one clown soldier, Tony’s shown the world there ain’t nothing scarier than a man who’s danced with fire, drank with devils, and still walks out carrying two bottles of Bacardi Rum one for him, and one for the poor soul catching an elbow to the face.

For 2 Tuff Tony, this ain’t just wrestling it’s a full-blown lifestyle. A non-stop death match with destiny, a beer-soaked saga of survival. And as long as Tony's still breathing (and chugging), his legend grows stronger than a stale Faygo bottle under a summer sun.

His work ethic? Ridiculous. His adaptability? Like a ninja in cargo shorts. His risk-taking? Let’s just say gravity’s caught more hands from Tony than half the JCW roster. That Grand Slam wasn’t just a win it was the payoff to years of blood, sweat, and hardcore carnage. Tony didn’t just collect titles…he broke the mold, shattered expectations, and redefined what it means to be the top dog in the underground circus of JCW.

7 Foot Tall Painful Paul.t:
Standing at a sky-scraping 7 feet, he's like a refrigerator with legs and a mean streak. One big boot from him and you're not just out of the ring — you're halfway to the parking lot wondering what dimension your teeth landed in.

With the St. Claire Monster Corporation disbanded, Painful Paul has found himself on his own... for now.

Alice Crowley.t:
Power. Grit. No apologies. That’s Big Al Alice Crowley, a former JCW Women’s Champion and one of the most savage forces to ever step into a Hatchet-ring. She ain’t here for hugs or high-fives—she’s here to throw hands, snap necks, and leave a trail of broken bodies with every bone-crunching brawl.

Blending raw aggression with fearless athleticism, Big Al has shattered bones, crushed egos, and straight-up moonsaulted over every expectation like it owed her money. She’s taken the JCW women’s division and turned it into a full-blown demolition derby.

While she’s already left Dani Mo staring up at the rafters in singles competition, Big Al’s path to the championship wasn’t exactly a fairy tale. More like a barbed-wire bedtime story. In a high-stakes three-way showdown, Crowley saw her shot, took it, and snatched that title like it was the last deep-fried Twinkie at the Gathering.

Sure, the win had a little controversy, but who cares? Big Al don’t need approval she needs chaos. Every time she steps into that ring, it’s a Juggalo-style statement: bring the pain or get stomped.

Backstage brawls? Yup. Suplexs into folding chairs? Check. Foreign objects flying like party favors? We’re not saying she did it but we’re not saying she didn’t. One thing’s for sure: this is her era, and she’s got the scars to prove it.

Big Al ain’t just a standout. She’s a standout killer in the JCW tradition loud, proud, and ready to drop elbows from the top rope straight into the clowniverse. Whoop whoop!

Backseat Boyz.t:
The Backseat Boyz originally with Johnny Kashmere and the late, great Trent Acid were one of the illest tag teams to blaze through the 2000s like a Faygo-fueled tornado. After Trent took that last ride to the Big Top in the sky in 2010, the team hit pause. But like a zombie clown at a midnight carnival, you can't keep a Backseat Boy down for long.

Fast forward to 2023, and Johnny Kashmere resurrected the Backseat Boyz back from the dead like a wicked necromancer, linkin’ up with the wild-as-hell Grayson brothers, JP and Tommy. Formerly known as The Amazing Graysons, these two debuted at Harpos in Detroit aka the Juggalo coliseum and straight-up jacked the JCW Tag Team Titles on sight marking the start of a powerful new chapter in the Backseat legacy.

Now rebranded and reborn as The Backseat Boyz 2.0, they ain’t just your average tag team, they’re Psychopathic. That’s right: they've partnered up with none other than Psychopathic Records, diving face first into music vids, event hosting, and whatever other flavor of chaos comes with that hatchet hustle.

And here’s where it gets even more whoop worthy: Violent J himself - yes, The Duke of the Wicked has taken on the role of ringside manager, guiding the Graysons through the tag team trenches. With J in their corner, these ninja warriors have defended the JCW Tag Titles coast-to-coast like it’s a nationwide Faygo spraying campaign.

Today, The Backseat Boyz are more than wrestlers they're rock stars with wrestling boots, Juggalos with powerbombs, and the torchbearers of a legacy that screams chaos, charisma, and clown love.

Barnabas the Bizarre.t:
Home Town: Splatter House, USA

Finisher: Fascination Street

Traveling across the stateside, a pre-vaudeville act began to capture the imagination of the masses. A unique blend of contortionism, acrobatics and showmanship made this pair of strapping young lads an instant hit amongst young and old alike. Especially on the United State’s East Coast, more specifically, Salem, Massachusetts. Dubbed the “Twins of Salem”, Jacksyn & Abel entertained the rich and poor, the sick and depraved, taking away the audiences troubles, even if just for a little while, with their astonishing acts of dare. That is, until fear and paranoia swept this quaint little town.

Accusations of witch craft arose, leading the Twins to be subject to a public execution for all to see. But before their lifeless bodies could be disposed, a rather peculiar on-looker intervened. A student of the occult, a practicing voodoo priestess, Elizabeth Laveau commandeered their lifeless bodies before desecration. The Twins were provided a ritualistic burial within the same New Orleans graveyard that would later become the final resting place of Elizabeth’s lineage, the Voodoo Queen herself, Marie Laveau.

Enter Barnabas the Bizarre, a collector, a historian of the odd, the different, the strange. Within his traveling Odditorium, he was in search of his next great “special attraction”. But within an era where the modern audience had in essence “seen everything”, Barnabas looked back to the past, to resurrect an act the world had not seen in hundreds of years. After paying a rather handsome sum to the descendants of the Laveau dynasty, the graves of the Twins of Salem were exhumed. A ritual to reanimate their lifeless corpses began, only, things took an unexpected turn for the worse. Instead of full reanimation, Jacksyn and Abel remain in an undead state, neither fully alive or dead. They exist merely to feast on the flesh, the brain matter of the living. And the only one who can control their insatiable hunger, is he who dared to dabble in the dark arts, all in the name of everlasting entertainment. A true carny through and through, Barnabas now presents the infected, the undead Twins of Salem, rechristened…The OUTBREAK

Brothers of Funstruction.t:
Step right up and witness the most twisted, terrifying, and totally unhinged tag team in JCW history! The Brothers of Funstruction, Yabo & Ruffo, aren’t just here to entertain—they’re here to destroy, dismember, and maybe steal your snacks while they're at it. These deranged jesters bring a chaotic mix of high-flying insanity, brute-force brawling, and twisted carnival mayhem, leaving a trail of broken opponents, shattered dreams, and exploded Faygo bottles in their wake.

Since crash-landing into JCW’s hardcore circus like a couple of clown-faced meteors, they’ve turned the tag team division into their own personal funhouse of destruction, complete with trapdoors, sledgehammers, and an occasional rubber cock beating. Their unpredictable style and relentless aggression have earned them tag team gold twice, proving that behind the face paint, squeaky noses, and wicked grins lies an unstoppable force of pure wrestling carnage.

Whether they’re juggling opponents in mid-air, cracking skulls like balloon animals, or turning the ring into their own demented bounce house of brutality, Yabo & Ruffo guarantee one thing—the fun never stops, the violence never sleeps, and the cotton candy’s always soaked in blood. Laugh now, cry later, The circus is in town!

Caleb Konley.t:
When 10 year old Caleb Konley first peeped ICP on ECW, it was like the heavens opened and sprayed him in the face with a two-liter of destiny. His two favorite things, underground music and pro wrestling collided in one glorious moment of mayhem, and that was it. The dude’s path was carved like a Hatchetman in a tree trunk.

As a teenager, Konley went full Jugga-maniac, diving headfirst into the horrorcore scene and the world of indy wrestling like he was cannonballing into a kiddie pool of Faygo. He obsessed over both until he became that guy, you know... the one who won’t shut up because he knows more than everybody else. And yeah, that ego grew like mold on an old wet pair of clown shoes.

Right after high school, Caleb hit up the 2005 Gathering for the JCW tryout, all hyped like he was gonna be the next Hatchet-wielding heavyweight. But then Mad Man Pondo hit him with the cold truth and told him he was the shits like, not even "funny shits," just plain ol’ stanky and that he needed real training. So Caleb took his bruised pride and that fiery Juggalo spirit, and hit wrestling schools from Atlanta to Charlotte, even over in Tokyo—like a ninja on a mission to earn his stripes.

Fast forward 20 years and this ninja’s been wreckin’ rings across five continents, snatching titles and contracts from some of the biggest feds in the game.

In 2024, with the launch of JCW Lunacy, Caleb finally came back home—back to where the spark first lit. And while he’s got mad skills in the ring, dude ain’t exactly handing out hugs and autographs. He became the first-ever American Champion, sure—but he’s also out here clowning fans, calling them a bunch of second-deck Juffs who don’t know jack about that old school wicked shit.

Cokane.t:
Known as the Devil’s Favorite Dealer, Cokane made his debut at JCW Devil’s Night with an explosive, electrifying presence that straight-up snorted the spotlight and left the crowd tweakin’. Fans got hooked instantly! Not just on his in-ring chaos, but on the pure, uncut madness he drips with. Cokane isn't just a wrestler he's a walking, talking overdose of destruction.

Cokane is addiction in motion, devastation in a pair of boots, and somehow...still stylish while doin’ it. A viral sensation in JCW, his climb to the top wasn’t greased with traditional wrestling holds it was built in the filthy, graffiti-tagged underbelly of the JCW Dark Carnival. That’s right he didn’t train in a gym, he leveled up in a funhouse mirror maze full of bats and bad decisions.

He’s not here to play nice. He’s here to twist the game like a balloon animal at a meth-head birthday party. He’s here to disrupt, dismantle, and rewire every thought you had about what wrestling is...then spike it off the turnbuckle.

Once you’ve been touched by Cokane, there’s no rehab, homie. He’s the Devil’s favorite for a reason. He don’t just beat you, he remixes your soul, piece by broken piece, and leaves you fiending for more.

The Devil’s Favorite Dealer isn’t just here to win; he’s here to leave his mark. Business is boomin’, and believe this: the first hit was free... but now you’re payin’ in blood.

Dani Mo.t:
In only a mere 5 years of professional wrestling, Dani Mo has carved out a name for herself as an energetic, fresh as fuck, and versatile performer. Known for not just being easy on the eyes, but also her high-flying maneuvers and charismatic presence. In 2024 she was ranked #109 in Pro Wrestling Illustrated's Top 250 women.

Dino-Myte Dani Mo made history in October of 2023 by becoming the first-ever JCW Women’s Champion, a true testament to her groundbreaking contributions to fucking these other bitches up! Since her debut in JCW it’s been very clear that Dani Mo is not just a fan favorite but also an unfuckwitable force which will leave all her competitors crying face down on the mat like the real baby bitch-asses they are.

Facts for facts sakes: Dani Mo holds the Guiness World Record for the highest altitude ever for a women's wrestling match. This historic event took place in May 2024 at an altitude of 18,519 feet above sea level, on Kala Patthar in the Nepal Himalayas near Mt. Everest. And incase that doesn’t register with you, that’s higher than Bushwick Bill running around the Gathering and claiming to hold the skull of Tupac Shakur.

Dani Mo's competitive drive and determination translate seamlessly into her in-ring performances, where she continues to captivate audiences with her vibrant persona and skill set. Whether she is competing in singles matches or in her tag team of The Neon Blondes, she remains a standout talent in the world of professional wrestling.

Jeff the Ref.t:
For nearly two decades, Jeff the Ref has had one of the hardest jobs in professional wrestling: trying to keep order in Juggalo Championship Wrestling.

While most referees are lucky if they make it through a match without getting flattened, screamed at, or both, Jeff has survived years of chaos, carnage, and situations where the rulebook probably should have included a few more pages. His knowledge of the game, quick decisions, and unmistakable smile have made him one of the most recognizable faces in JCW.

Jeff the Ref has officiated some of the biggest matches in independent wrestling, including EVOLVE 131 live on the WWE Network, but nothing compares to the madness that comes with stepping between two wrestlers in the JCW Arena.

When he's not keeping the peace in the ring, Jeff stays busy behind the scenes at Psychopathic Records. Whether he's holding the ropes open for a ring girl or holding a wrestler back from doing something stupid, JCW knows one thing: if Jeff the Ref is there, somebody is trying to ruin his day.

Joe Dombrowski.t:
Pro Wrestling broadcaster for over 22 years, Joe Dombrowski has called around 9,000 matches across the globe...yeah, that’s nine thousand times he’s yelled “WHAT A MOVE!” while chaos unfolded in front of him. From Ring of Honor to AAA to Big Japan, he's seen more piledrivers than your average chiropractor. But outside of JCW, he’s best known as the lead voice of Major League Wrestling aka the guy who makes body slams sound like Shakespeare.

Beyond the mic, Dombrowski's dipped his toes into film work too—producing gems like The Montreal Theory and The Legend of Virgil & His Traveling Merchandise Table (yes, that’s a real thing, and yes, it's as wild as it sounds).

He’s also a wrestling historian on a mission, digging through VHS stacks and dusty basements like a detective with a mullet, preserving the lost and rare footage of legends who paved the way some with honor, others with chairs wrapped in barbed wire.

Armed with knowledge, passion, and a sixth sense for surviving pure mayhem, Joe fits right in as one of the main voices of JCW Lunacy. He’s the calm in the storm…right before someone gets hit upside there nugget with a stop sign!

Kerry Morton.t:
Kerry Morton is a sniveling baby, talented enough to avoid trying hard and riding the coattails of his legendary pops, Ricky Morton. This ninja was practically born in a headlock and still manages to slither out of real competition like a greasy carnie con man. Sure, he’s a naturally gifted athlete, but instead of flexin’ those skills, he’d rather pay off henchmen, ghost his tag partners, and take more shortcuts than a GPS on bath salts.

Morton’s already left his greasy fingerprints all over the ring as a former NWA World Junior Heavyweight Champion and has been a thorn in JCW’s side as one-third of the Southern Six. He even snagged some JCW Tag Team gold with James Storm—until Storm realized riding with Kerry was like putting your faith in a leaky Faygo bottle.

Kerry claims he’s got a rock solid background in amateur wrestling as a former state champ, and that he mixes technical skills with high-flyin’ swagger to create some wild mutant style in the ring. We ain’t denying the kid’s got moves but he’s also got the ego of three Ric Flairs stacked in a trench coat.

He calls himself the Rizz God which we assume means he’s mastered the art of making people hate him while thinking they love him. Whether he’s stalling in the ropes like a scared little bitch or tossing a mule kick to the nuggets while the ref’s looking the other way, Kerry Morton’s convinced he’s proving the future of pro wrestling is in his soft, entitled hands. He even demands fans refer to him as Mr. JCW from now on. Sure buddy, we’ll do that just as soon as you finishes eating a giant bowl of dicks.

Immigrating from the old country sometime in the 2010s, Luigi Primo began wrestling in 2013. Backed by a lifetime of martial arts and culinary training, this dough-slingin’ ninja brought more than just sauce to the table. As a line cook in pizza joints across Austin, Texas, Luigi leveled up his pizza skills while fending off the chaos that comes with being a low-wage kitchen warrior—think hot grease, sharp knives, and the occasional drunk customer trying to square up over cold breadsticks.

Catching hands and tossing dough, Primo had an epiphany: why not blend his passions for pizza and pummeling into one fresh-baked masterpiece? Thus, PIZZA WRESTLING was born, half combat sport, half culinary chaos, all flavor.

Everything Luigi Primo does in the ring mirrors his pizza-making process: tenderizing opponents with holds like they’re unruly dough, slicing fools up with knife-edge chops that’d make a pepperoni cry, and yes literally hurling pizza dough at them like a saucy tornado. It was this last move that launched Luigi into viral stardom in 2022, when the internet caught wind of his cheesy reversals and couldn’t look away.

Since then, Luigi’s taken his pie-slingin’ style international, wrestling in Japan, Canada, and Thailand, and even throwing dough twice on AEW TV. But don’t get it twisted like a breadstick, Luigi ain't just a walking meme. He’s a legit technician in the ring, flipping between clean combos and full-body smacks like he’s flipping pies during a Friday night rush.

At JCW, Luigi’s finally found the perfect proving ground, a place where he can showcase that he’s not only the best pizza chef this side of Little Italy, but also a battle-ready beast fit for clown royalty. That’s amore, Whoop Whoop!

Dubbed the “Twins of Salem”, Jacksyn & Abel entertained the rich and poor, the sick and depraved, taking away the audiences troubles, even if just for a little while, with their astonishing acts of dare. That is, until fear and paranoia swept this quaint little town.

Accusations of witch craft arose, leading the Twins to be subject to a public execution for all to see. But before their lifeless bodies could be disposed, a rather peculiar on-looker intervened. A student of the occult, a practicing voodoo priestess, Elizabeth Laveau commandeered their lifeless bodies before desecration. But within an era where the modern audience had in essence “seen everything”, Barnabas looked back to the past, to resurrect an act the world had not seen in hundreds of years. After paying a rather handsome sum to the descendants of the Laveau dynasty, the graves of the Twins of Salem were exhumed. A ritual to reanimate their lifeless corpses began, only, things took an unexpected turn for the worse. Instead of full reanimation, Jacksyn and Abel remain in an undead state, neither fully alive or dead. They exist merely to feast on the flesh, the brain matter of the living. And the only one who can control their insatiable hunger, is he who dared to dabble in the dark arts, all in the name of everlasting entertainment. A true carny through and through, Barnabas now presents the infected, the undead Twins of Salem, rechristened…The OUTBREAK

Richie Boy Breyer Wellington is a former two time JCW Heavyweight Champion and the first man to pick up a victory on the first ever live JCW pay-per-view. Victory for him isn’t just about winning—it’s about making his opponents and the fans alike understand that no one could possibly match his self-professed stature, sophistication, or wealth.

Attending his first wrestling show at only 3 weeks old and making his in-ring debut at the tender age of 4, Colby Corino claims the title of the youngest veteran in professional wrestling at just 28. This 2nd generation superstar (or “super dick,” depending on who you ask! Was damn near born in a wrestling ring, probably suplexed out of the womb.

Following in the boot prints of his legendary father, “The King of Old School” Steve Corino, “The Prince of Old School” is dead set on dragging the lost art of true professional wrestling back into the spotlight kicking and screaming like a drunk ninja at the Gathering. He detests colorful gimmicks and can’t stand the over-the-top showmanship now clogging up locker rooms like a port-a-potty on Day 3 at the Gathering. To him, there’s no place for glitter, glow sticks, or dancing mascots in this sport unless it’s to powerbomb them into extinction.

While his bloodline is stacked with accolades, Colby’s carved out his own legacy across the globe, battling in some of the top promotions out there. But it’s JCW that really fires up his disdain-powered engine. Why? In his own words: “JCW has no end of the exact type of gimmicky bullshit I hate. So I find plenty of extra incentive to kick major ass left and right in this stupid clown company."

He’s on a mission to surgically remove every trace of tomfoolery from JCW like it’s a bad tattoo, declaring that by the time he’s done, JCW will stand for “Just Colby Wrestling.” Corino's sights are locked on the JCW World Heavyweight Championship, not for the fame, but to show the whole damn circus what a real professional wrestling champion is supposed to look like.

He’s still out here wildin’ out, defying gravity, and makin’ crowds chant “Whoop whoop!” every time he steps through the curtain. Jasmin St. Claire.t:
Led by the wickedly twisted Jasmin St. Claire, the unholy hat trick of Kongo Kong, Seven Foot Tall Painful Paul, and the walking fever dream known as Mr. Happy have been raising hell in JCW since crash-landing in Las Vegas like a clown car from the underworld.

Ain’t nobody knows where Mr. Happy came from — rumor is he was once a kid’s birthday clown who snapped harder than a glow stick in the pit after a family tragedy. Now he’s just a walking grin with a chainsaw heart. He got the name “Mr. Happy” thanks to the permanent Joker-smile scrawled across his mug, but don’t let the name fool ya — he’s about as cuddly as a barbed-wire teddy bear. No empathy, no remorse, just pure party-fueled pain and chaos.

Kongo Kong? That dude’s not even human — more like a pissed-off kaiju with a mohawk. He didn’t hold the JCW Heavyweight Championship for 953 days to make friends; he did it to turn bones to powder and dreams to nightmares.

And then there’s Painful Paul. Standing at a sky-scraping 7 feet, he’s like a refrigerator with legs and a mean streak. One big boot from him and you're not just out of the ring — you’re halfway to the parking lot wondering what dimension your teeth landed in.

St. Claire, with her roots in ECW’s chaos garden, says her monsters needed someone smart, savage, and stone-cold twisted to guide 'em — someone who could turn their hunger for violence into a fine art. And so she did. The result? A living, breathing freak show that doesn’t just break the rules — they eat the rulebook and spit it back out with glitter and blood.

Mad Man Pondo.t:
A straight-up war god of blood-soaked rings and barbed-wire nightmares, Mad Man Pondo ain’t just etched into the annals of hardcore wrestling—he chainsawed his name in with a rusty blade. This man’s career is built on broken glass, flaming tables, and questionable life choices shouted from a crowd of face-painted lunatics screaming “WHOOP WHOOP!”

He’s a certified JCW legend—two-time World Heavyweight Champion, three-time Tag Team Champion (twice with human meat grinder Necro Butcher, once with the chaos pixie Crazy Mary Dobson)—and probably the only guy to win an exploding barbed wire match and still hit up a Waffle House that same night.

Pondo straight-up blew the roof off JCW from the jump—literally—by winning an exploding barbed wire match at the very first JCW show teaming with Pete Madden to blow up Ian Rotten and Corporal Robinson like a meth lab in a trailer park horror movie. Since then, he’s had feuds so brutal with Necro and 2 Tuff Tony, even Freddy Krueger took notes. His appearances at Bloodymania? Legendary. Glass was shattered, blood was spilled, and somebody’s uncle probably got hit with a stop sign.

But don’t get it twisted under all the scars, blood, and unexplainable smells, Pondo’s been a mentor to a new generation of JCW sickos, teaching them the fine art of pain, pride, and how to properly set a dude on fire without missing your cue.

He’s not just a veteran. He’s JCW’s duct-taped, barbed-wired, blood-slicked heart, still beatin’ after all these years. And if you ain’t down with that—catch him in the ring. He’s got a stop sign with your name on it, ninja.

Mark Roberts.t:
Mark Roberts is the reincarnation of a circus press agent. The old days of Athletic Shows on sawdust and elephant shit run through his veins, and promoting the mat game has been his preoccupation for as since he was shot out of his fathers nut sack.

His first foray into pro wrestling came when he was a teenager on New York City's wrestling hotlines. After a false start attempting to be the underage voice of Bobby Lombardi's Long Island Wrestling Federation, he moved to the Pacific Northwest and studied journalism.

He returned to wrestling in 2019 and made his ring announcing debut for Impact Wrestling in 2020. He has filled every broadcasting role in Rhino's Insane Wrestling Revolution and now calls Detroit home. With a deep love of wrestling history, and a reporter's attention to detail, he strives to guide wrestling fans through the carnival of carnage that is JCW.

Since coming on board at Spanksgivin', Roberts has formed a close bond with colleague Zac Amico, with whom he shares an obsessive knowledge of the Tina Fey sitcom 30 Rock. He also enjoys arguing with Joe Dombrowski about the virtues and flaws of pro wrestling journalism. When not on the road, he studies old JCW tapes, collects bottles on the freeway, and reads too much political news.

Matt Cross.t:
From the backyard to the big time, there has never, and will never, be another Matt Cross. In a recent article, Forbes.com said Cross "may well be the most well traveled professional wrestler in the world." Having wrestled in 28 countries, and 47 states, one

could certainly make a convincing argument.

Bursting onto the scene as MDogg20, and garnering instant notoriety for his backyard antics, he was immortalized on the front cover of the "Backyard Wrestling: Don't Try This at Home' video game where, alongside ICP, he's a playable character.

Matt then leapt directly from your favorite console, into the world of the Insane Clown Posse, debuting at the 'JCW: Volume 3' DVD Taping where the middle rope infamously snapped, plummeting him violently to the ground below. Rallied on by the raucous fans in attendance, Matt crawled back to his feet, managed to get in the ring, and through sheer will and determination finished the match, cementing his place in the hallowed halls of JCW lore.

With no signs of slowing down, over 25 years of experience, and a JCW Heavyweight Title Reign under his belt, it's safe to say this veteran has his sights set on JCW Gold because wrestling is forever and Matt Cross is forever!

Step back in time with Mr. 50’s Myles Clark, the living embodiment of the rugged and raw spirit of the 1950s. A newcomer to JCW, but a seasoned veteran of the squared circle, Clark brings an old-school charm to modern wrestling that’s impossible to ignore.

Hailing from an era when men were tough and the stakes were higher, Mr. 50’s doesn’t just wrestle – he represents a bygone time where grit, toughness, and style mattered above all.

A true chain-smoking, chain-wrestling grappler, Clark is always impeccably dressed in vintage 50’s attire, rocking the fashion and flair of a classic era. Whether it’s his sharp suits, slicked-back hair, or smooth moves in the ring, this wrestler is as authentic as Russian snake charmer.

When Mr. 50’s enters the ring, the atmosphere changes. His very presence makes the screen flicker and turn black and white, as if the audience is transported to a golden era of professional wrestling. Don’t let his old-school demeanor fool you – he’s a modern-day force to be reckoned with. Mr. 50’s Myles Clark is here to show that some things only get better with age.

Ain’t nobody knows where Mr. Happy came from — rumor is he was once a kid’s birthday clown who snapped harder than a glow stick in the pit after a family tragedy. Now he’s just a walking grin with a chainsaw heart. He got the name “Mr. Happy” thanks to the permanent Joker-smile scrawled across his mug, but don’t let the name fool ya — he’s about as cuddly as a barbed-wire teddy bear. No empathy, no remorse, just pure party-fueled pain and chaos.

Kongo Kong? That dude’s not even human — more like a pissed-off kaiju with a mohawk. He didn’t hold the JCW Heavyweight Championship for 953 days to make friends; he did it to turn bones to powder and dreams to nightmares.

And then there’s Painful Paul. Standing at a sky-scraping 7 feet, he’s like a refrigerator with legs and a mean streak. One big boot from him and you're not just out of the ring — you’re halfway to the parking lot wondering what dimension your teeth landed in.

St. Claire, with her roots in ECW’s chaos garden, says her monsters needed someone smart, savage, and stone-cold twisted to guide 'em — someone who could turn their hunger for violence into a fine art. And so she did. The result? A living, breathing freak show that doesn’t just break the rules — they eat the rulebook and spit it back out with glitter and blood.

Officer Colt Cabana.t:
Bitch ass Officer Colt Cabana has gone undercover on the international wrestling scene holding multiple titles while also starring on the national hit TV show COPS for more than two decades. Most know him as innovator in merchandising and podcasting as well as a superior technical wrestler. But his true passion is his thick blue line.

Officer Cabana was given the assignment to clean up the Detroit gang scene in 2010. Along with the brave and handsome heroes of the FBI, he’s been in pursuit of Juggalo dismantlement ever since. Currently boasting to well over 1,726 Juggalo arrests, Officer Piggie Pie…. I mean Cabana is a true hero in the eyes of none.

A former Juggalo Heavyweight Champion, he cheaply defeated 2 Tuff Tony for that coveted prize before dropping it a mere one week later. He has been a key part of the JCW roster and ruining everyones fun for more than 15 years.

His goal: Arrest and rehabilitate every single Juggalo in the country, and dismantle Juggalo Championship Wrestling from the inside out.

Ricky Morton.t:
A true legend of the squared circle, Ricky Morton is the embodiment of heart, hustle, and high-flying excitement. As one-half of the legendary Rock ‘n’ Roll Express, Morton

redefined tag team wrestling with his lightning-fast offense, unmatched resilience, and an uncanny ability to rally a crowd like no other.

His battles against the biggest and baddest in the industry cemented his legacy as one of pro wrestling’s greatest underdogs—and one of its toughest survivors. He's wrestled everywhere from Jim Crockett Promotions to Frontier Martial-Arts Wrestling, and from Mid-South to Extreme Championship Wrestling.

But Morton’s influence extends beyond classic rivalries and iconic matches. He made his JCW debut in Volume 1, proving that rock ‘n’ roll never dies and neither does his

fighting spirit. After nearly defeating Evil Dead to become the first ever JCW World Champion, Morton is back and looking for gold.

Unlike Evil Dead, rock ‘n’ roll will never die, and neither will Ricky Morton.

Shane Mercer.t:
Shane Mercer has been tearing up the wrestling scene around the world for 18 years. From GCW to MLW to ZERO1 in Japan, Mercer has shown his agility, power and technical prowess. He was recently name dropped on Raw when Logan Paul shamelessly stole his finisher. Apparently Paul doesn’t know who he’s fucking with.

Mercer climbed to the pinnacle of JCW defeating Kongo Kong for the heavyweight championship at Bloodymania 12 and holding it for more than a year. After losing the title, he vanished from JCW for more than five years – only to come back in the Lunacy era.

This time around, Mercer has a different goal Motivated only by money and as violent as ever, he has become a mercenary for anyone who will cough up the funds to have him do their bidding. Cough up the cash, he’ll whoop some ass!

Corino acquired Mercer's services to help him win the JCW world tag team championships – only to be told Mercer expected to be paid to defend the titles, causing them to be vacated. The lesson should be clear – Mercer can handle anyone in the ring, but he expects to be paid cold hard cash. No credit cards bitch!

Steven Flowe.t:
Steven Flowe is more than just a wrestler he’s a grunge-drenched, flannel-flying freakshow resurrecting the rebellious spirit of the '90s, one body slam at a time. Debuting with the Super Wrestlers in September 2024, Flowe didn’t just dip a toe in – nah, this ninja cannonballed straight into the deep end, winning his first match in front of a hyped Chicago crowd that popped harder than a Faygo bottle at the Gathering.

The vibe? As raw and nasty as a Nirvana riff played in a haunted carnival. With an entrance that lit up social media like the Tilt-a-Whirl on fire, Flowe didn’t just bring grunge back he dragged it outta the grave, slapped some facepaint on it, and handed it a steel chair.

Now the whole damn world is chanting "Steven Flowe," as his music-blasted, mosh-pit-chaotic energy hooks both wrestling heads and old-school flannel freaks. But this ain’t just about wrestling moves it’s about the culture, the chaos, it’s about the art.

Now, the “Super Wrestlers Phenomenon” crashes into JCW Lunacy like a stage-diving maniac with a mission. He’s here to throw down with the Juggalos and Juggalettes, ready to tear up the ring like it owes him money. Trained the gritty way in a boxing ring that probably smelled like sweat, cigarettes, and broken dreams, Flowe might look like your cousin who never left the garage band phase but don’t get it twisted. He’s the grunge hero wrestling didn’t know it needed… but the Juggalos sure as hell deserve.

Violent J.t:
From the Dark Carnival to the blood-splattered ring, Violent J is more than just a founding father of Juggalo Championship Wrestling he’s the crusty, painted-up soul of it. Now rockin’ the badge of Commissioner like a stolen backstage pass, the Duke of the Wicked runs JCW with an iron fist shoved deep in a clown glove that’s probably still sticky from last month’s main event. He ain’t here to make friends he’s here to make sure the chaos flows like cheap nacho cheese at a county fair.

As one half of the multi-platinum selling band Insane Clown Posse, J didn’t just help birth JCW he straight-up yanked it out of the underground kicking and screaming like a gremlin in a bar fight. He built a haven for hardcore freaks, misfit warriors, and wrestlers who think a tetanus shot is just part of the pre-match warmup. If you’re lookin’ for rules and order, you’re about 17 exits past the wrong place.

Now, as Commissioner, he’s calling the shots, setting the matches, and delivering twisted justice straight from the Dark Carnival playbook if that playbook was handwritten on the back of a greasy burrito wrapper during a bender. One minute he’s laying down the law, the next he’s flipping the script like a pancake on parole. You never know what’s coming and that’s exactly how he likes it.

You may not agree with his decisions but you will respect them. Or he’ll book you in a match against a guy named Chainsaw Chuck and a shopping cart full of mousetraps. He’s the voice of the wicked, the law of the land, and the heartbeat of JCW. All hail The Duke and maybe watch your back... especially if it’s Monday, full moon, or just ‘cause he feels like it.

Willie Mack.t:
Willie Mack didn’t come from privilege—nah, homie was forged in the concrete jungle of South Central Los Angeles. He’s a straight-up product of struggle, survival, and a spirit tougher than a rusty hatchet. While other fools let the streets chew 'em up and spit 'em out, Mack flipped the script turnin’ all that pain, rage, and hood energy into a one-man wreckin’ crew that couldn’t be ignored.

A two-time JCW Heavyweight Champion, Mack ain't just a beast he's a chocolate-covered wrecking ball with the agility of a ninja on a sugar high. One minute he’s flyin’ through the air like he’s got hidden wings, the next he’s slammin’ fools into the mat like a ton of bricks soaked in Faygo. Powerbombs, moonsaults, elbow drops from another dimension! This ninja can do it all.

But what really sets Willie apart is that untamed aggression and that deep, bone-level Juggalo pride. This ain’t just a gimmick it’s life. It's who he is. He don’t just rep the Hatchet...he lives it. The JCW locker room’s already been put on high alert they're ain’t no clownin’ around when Mack steps through those ropes. For anyone brave (or dumb) enough to face him, it ain’t just a match it’s a straight-up trip through the Dark Carnival.

So when that bell rings, you either bow down to the Chocolate Juggalo…or you get stomped out like a stale bag of cotton candy. Mack ain’t playin’ games, he ain’t got time for sideshows he’s here to defend not just his belt, but his legacy and the entire Juggalo nation. And believe this: ain't no so-called “kings” or “legends” safe when Willie Mack's in the ring... because this ninja came to dominate or detonate.

Beast Man.t: Official JCW roster member. Catch them every Thursday night on JCW Lunacy.

Big Vito.t:
Big Vito has been a problem for JCW and Violent J since the moment he walked in the door. Sent by new JCW investor Vince Russo to "protect the investment", Vito quickly took matters into his own hands by misrepresenting his authority and being a complete prick to anyone he crossed paths with. Vito's mission was clear. He wanted the Juggalos removed from JCW. No more clown makeup. No more Faygo. No more Violent J. There would be rules and respect.

After failing to gain Violent J's power for himself after what he considers a betrayal by Russo, Vito decided to bring in the family — his family — The Luciano Family. With his right hand man Vincenzo and his nephew Sally Boy by his side, Vito has a renewed focus with everyone in JCW in his crosshairs.

Oh, and that dress business? He was under investigation.

Choppa City.t:
Bruce Wayans is good at getting into sticky situations and dragging his usually worried tag partner Atiba along for the ride.

Choppa City gained a tryout in JCW thanks to their past dealings with JCW Co-Owner Vince Russo. However on the day of their tryout, they decided to skip the line and immediately insert themselves into a cage match between The Brothers of Funstruction and The Outbreak. This plan backfired, and Choppa City were out the door as fast as they entered.

A second "chopportunity" in JCW came after they got booked on Lunacy by fooling Russo and claiming they were a different well-known tag team. History did not repeat itself as Choppa City made a positive impression by winning matches, earning themselves a spot on the roster and eventually becoming JCW World Tag Team Champions.

If Wayans can stay focused and keep himself and Atiba out of trouble, Choppa City may be the Tag Team to beat in JCW for years to come.

Disco Ray.t: Official JCW roster member. Catch them every Thursday night on JCW Lunacy.

EC3.t:
Ethan Carter III is no stranger to having family members inside the wrestling business. With his second cousin Jeeves already here, the duo struck a deal with Violent J to bring "The Top 1%" to JCW.

He made an immediate impact as the Special Guest Referee for the JCW Lunacy World Championship match at Strangle-Mania, while earning a bullseye on his back courtesy of Vince Russo and "The Chosen One" Caleb Konley. EC3 has been fighting an uphill battle to stay healthy and competitive in JCW ever since with Russo doing everything he can to send him packing.

Having the determination and work ethic that few possess, EC3 will not stop until he is World Champion once again — this time in JCW, no matter what Russo puts in his way.

Father Bronson.t:
He's taught us how to make hot tea, how to get rid of problems, how to make candles and lotions, and how to turn a bully into a friend. However there is much unknown about the mysterious Father Bronson. He claims to have learned patience through "Red Love" ever since he was a child, bouncing from home to home due to not having parents in his life.

While he portrays himself as someone delivering a positive message, there appears to be dark secrets hidden in the many sermons of "Red Love". While many wonder what exactly "Red Love" is all about, some of those answers may be best left in the past.

Gisele Shaw.t:
A multi-time Champion around the globe, Gisele Shaw earned a contract in JCW by winning a Best-of-Three series against Freya the Slaya, who was being used by "Broke Ass" Breyer Wellington for his own personal gain.

Shaw's first order of business as a member of the JCW Roster was taking on Wellington, who she defeated. Now, "The Quintessential Diva" has her sights set on the JCW Women's World Championship.

Hokane.t:
Hokane arrived in JCW as Cokane's #1 fan, sitting in the front row cheering on her favorite wrestler behind a mask of her own. One night following a victory, Cokane noticed her in the crowd and rewarded her fandom by giving her a giant bag of powder from his stash. What was a kind gesture from a wrestler to their fan quickly turned into a parasocial obsession. Hokane became jealous over a professional bond between Cokane and Alice Crowley, breaking into the backstage area and attacking Crowley on several occasions.

After failing to gain affection from Cokane and left gasping for air by a beat down from Crowley, Barnabas the Bizarre welcomed Hokane into his family as she now looks to carve her own path in JCW.

Hollyhood Haley J.t:
“The Boujhettoest Baddie” became an overnight sensation on Netflix due to her “give no fucks” attitude. Taking what she learned from 2 Tuff Tony and her mother The Amazing Maria, Haley J turned that into a Championship career almost instantly, winning the JCW Women's World Championship after an intense feud with Alice Crowley.

She's rude and she's loud, using that to her advantage to get inside the heads of her opponents. But when the bell rings, she'll beat your ass.

Don't turn your back on her, or you might get hit with a sock full of rocks.

James Storm.t:
“Sorry about your damn luck” to anyone who has to step in the ring with “The Cowboy” James Storm.

Known to have a beer or two before (or during) his matches, Storm continues to add success to his already legendary career, including winning the JCW World Tag Team Championship with Kerry Morton during his brief alliance with The Southern Six.

Storm suffered a serious knee injury at the hands of Mr. Anderson, but is now fully recovered and looking for more gold in JCW.

Joel Gertner.t:
He's the Quintessential Stud Muffin and an ECW Legend. WWE named him one of the 50 Greatest Talkers of all-time. But that's not enough for Joel Gertner because he wants to add some Lunacy to his Legacy.

Still recovering from a neck injury he suffered in 1997, Gertner arrived in JCW with former JCW World Champion Josh Bishop, dubbing him "Big Money" and making the claim that he is still a rightful World Champion after he was stripped of his Championship years ago by Violent J.

Gertner may have a big mouth, but he backs up his talk. With Big Money and Legacy driving him forward in JCW, we're about to see his biggest successes yet in his monumental career.

Josh Bishop.t:
1 of 1. The Intense Icon. Big Money. Josh Bishop is everything you look for in a pro wrestler... unless you're standing across the ring from him.

Bishop won the JCW World Championship in 2023, but he only had a handful of title defenses before being stripped of the Championship by Violent J after he was unable to attend the premiere episode of JCW Lunacy. Bishop, in response, left JCW.

He made a surprise return to JCW in 2026, bringing the Championship with him that he never lost in the ring, as well as ECW Legend "The Quintessential Stud Muffin" Joel Gertner to help guide him back to the top. Violent J and Vince Russo agreed to reinstate Bishop as a rightful JCW Champion, adding a second major Championship to JCW. But that isn't enough to satisfy Bishop and Gertner, as they look to take the JCW Lunacy World Championship and unify it with their Championship.

Mecha Wolf.t:
Known for both his power and speed, Mecha Wolf is the kind of predator who never stops chasing for long. When he's not fronting a horror metal band, he's making enough noise inside the ring to wake the dead.

The international standout has battled across the world, bringing a bruising style and ruthless attitude everywhere he goes. Whether he's launching himself through the air or driving an opponent into the mat, Mecha Wolf has a nasty habit of making every fight feel like a pack hunt.

JCW fans have watched him wage smashmouth wars with Shane Mercer and battle for both the American and world championships. Around here, Mecha Wolf is never far from title contention — and if history has taught us anything, it's that a hungry wolf doesn't stay hungry forever.

Nic Nemeth.t:
Nic Nemeth is the definition of a professional, inside and out of the ring. A World Champion in multiple organizations, Nemeth would love to add the JCW Lunacy World Championship to his resume.

"The Wanted Man" has flown the JCW flag high and proud since he became part of the family, fighting for JCW in The 2 Day War against GCW as well as for Team Violent J against Team Vito.

Ninja Mack.t:
If you blink during a Ninja Mack match, you're probably going to miss something that shouldn't be physically possible.

Armed with a seemingly endless supply of flips, dives, and aerial insanity, Ninja Mack has built a reputation as one of the most jaw-dropping high flyers in wrestling today. With victories over Caleb Konley and Kerry Morton, the former American champion wrestles like he's trying to unlock secret levels in the laws of physics.

Of course, living life several feet above the ring comes with a simple rule: what goes up eventually comes down. The problem for Ninja Mack's opponents is figuring out exactly where he's coming down before it's too late.

Whether he's soaring through the air or crashing into somebody's chest from impossible angles, one thing is certain. When Ninja Mack is on the card, gravity is less of a law and more of a suggestion.

PCO.t: Official JCW roster member. Catch them every Thursday night on JCW Lunacy.

Sonny Kiss.t:
Sonny Kiss is a former professional cheerleader and award-winning dancer who hit the wrestling scene at just 17 as a valet — but don’t get it twisted, she wasn’t just carryin’ jackets, she was scoping the game and plotting her rise like a true ring ninja. Two years later, she made her in-ring debut, and by 2018, she was flipping fools and dazzling crowds on national TV with Lucha Underground.

A founding member of AEW’s roster, Sonny’s been coast-to-coast across the US and Canada, droppin’ jaws with her bubbly, high-energy style, jaw-dropping moveset, and athleticism that straight-up floats like Faygo fizz rivaling the wildest high-flyers in the biz. A protégé of the legendary Dustin Rhodes (aka Goldust with extra glitter), Sonny’s now an 11-year vet who's danced, dropped, and dazzled her way onto the biggest stages in the game.

Now, this fierce and fabulous trailblazer has her wicked eyes locked on the JCW Women’s Championship. And best believe, she’s lookin’ to snatch that gold from inaugural champ Dani Mo like a ninja vanishin’ with your last Faygo all with a smile that’ll knock your domepiece into the astral plane.

Southern Six.t:
Southern Six (Alex Taylor, Kerry Morton & Silas Mason)

“Whiskey-fueled violence, Southern-born supremacy, and no damn apologies — served up hotter than a possum stew at a family reunion.”

From the great and grimy state of Tennessee, the Southern Six ain’t just a team — they’re a full-blown hoedown of haymakers and head trauma. A violent sermon preached by the unholy trinity of Alex Taylor, Kerry Morton, and Silas Mason. And to Juggalos everywhere? These boys are a living, breathing, steel-toed boot to the face of decency.

If wrestling had a redneck, southern-fried, moonshine-soaked outlaw biker gang, these boys would be the kings of the dirt road — flippin’ the bird to tradition, crushin’ skulls like Faygo cans under a four-wheeler.

Alex Taylor (Too Hot to Trot) – The Southern Shotgun. Quick on the draw and even quicker to talk that spicy trailer-park trash. He’s got fists like cinder blocks and a mouth that never learned manners.

Kerry Morton (Mr. JCW) – Wrestling royalty with a rockstar strut and a mullet blessed by the gods of chaos. Legacy? Yeah. Ego? Bigger than a Bigfoot sighting at The Gathering. He don’t just talk trash, he gift-wraps it and hands it to you in the middle of the ring.

Silas Mason – The Thrillbilly Juggernaut – A six-foot-plus slab of Appalachian vengeance. This man don’t wrestle. He stampedes. Built like a moonshine still and hits like one fell on you. He’s the power, the pain, and the reason the ring crew needs hazard pay.

Together, they are Southern Six, and they live by three sacred commandments:

Raise Hell. Break Necks. Leave with the Check.

They don’t make ‘em like this anymore… and that’s probably a good thing. One Southern Six beatdown is enough to make a ninja rethink their life choices.

Tarzan Duran.t:
Tarzan crawled outta the jungle, only to find out real quick that people suck! So he peaced out back to the jungle and leveled up into a straight-up demigod, doin’ his own thing with some off-the-grid, bushwhackin’ pagan rituals. Tarzan swears up and down he be choppin' it up with demons from both realms—earthside and the wicked beyond—through a flaming portal he built with elbow grease and questionable sanity.

For kicks, Tarzan writes banger tracks with these demons by bleeding all over some bark and lettin’ their ghostly hands spell out lyrics in the red sauce. Dark Juggalo poetry, straight from the jungle scrolls.

And when that full moon hits? You know Tarzan’s front row with the spirits, doin’ the Devil’s two-step at every underground bash from the back alleys of Tijuana to blood-soaked wrestling rings across the states. Every time he spills some crimson in the squared circle, it feeds the Devil's appetite just enough to keep the world spinnin’ for one more wicked day.

The Wraith.t:
The WRAITH is an enigma wrapped in shadow, a reflection of the Sixth Jokers Card—The Wraith, also known as Death. This dark and malevolent figure is not

merely a wrestler, but a living embodiment of the impending reckoning that comes to collect those who have spent their lives consumed by guilt and regret.

He is a harbinger, a final messenger of judgment, a chilling force of nature that only appears to those who are at the end of their road. The WRAITH emerged from the shadows of the dark carnival, a place where time holds no sway, to bring justice to the unjust, and to ensure that the guilty will face their eternal punishment.

Some say The WRAITH is a spirit, cursed to wander between the realms of the living and the dead. Others believe he is a man, one who has seen the ugliness of the world and been irrevocably transformed by it. His sole mission: To remind the world that every sin will be paid for in the end.

The WRAITH is not just a man—he is a storm, and his fighting style is a blend of vicious, relentless strikes, mind games, and eerie psychological warfare. The WRAITH is known for his psychological domination in the ring, often using his eerie presence and cryptic taunts to unnerve his opponents before unleashing brutal and calculated violence.

Vincenzo.t:
Vincenzo Benjamino is the loyal right hand to The Don of the Luciano Family, Big Vito. Vito put Vincenzo in charge of keeping his nephew Sally Boy in line, which is easier said than done. Vito is usually unhappy with Vincenzo's inability to keep Sally Boy out of trouble, constantly threatening to put him on the first boat back to Italy.

Vincenzo is a powerful and proven veteran inside the ring, but the full-time distraction of trying to keep Sally Boy out of trouble has cost him any kind of success in JCW so far.

Young Alter Boys.t:
Since the beginning of their careers in 2019, Bang and Matthews have been teaming together across the country, spreading dropkicks and questionable fashion choices wherever they roam. They've popped up in GCW, ROH, and even AEW Collision basically everywhere except your mom’s backyard (but that’s probably next).

While normally cheered, in JCW Bang and Matthews weren’t quite as loved by the Juggalo fanbase. Turns out, painting your faces and preaching about salvation doesn’t go over too well when half the crowd’s still recovering from Faygo showers and wicked clown rituals. So Bang and Matthews did what any rational tag team would do they went full holy roller and set out to save every Juggalo soul from its dark carnival destiny.

After scrapping with the BackSeat Boyz all up and down the Train of Terror tour, Bang and Matthews decided fists weren’t enough. So they busted out a Bible l, not to read, but to smite. One holy thump later, they were the new JCW tag team champions. And in the most unholy twist of fate, Johnny Kashmere betrayed the BackSeat Boyz, joined the unholy duo, and dubbed them the Young Alter Boys.

Now that the Young Alter Boys have had a taste of JCW gold (which they definitely didn’t bless first), they’re hell-bent on getting it back and saving the souls of Juggalos one backbreaker and awkward baptism at a time.

Instagram: @DaveyBang, @Getauggie

Abdullah the Butcher.t: Abdullah partook in JCW Volume 1, 2 & 3 in three epic clashes vs The Rude Boy, including once in a steel cage. He also appeared on several Bloodymania cards, including once vs Jake The Snake & Pogo The Clown where he never even got into the ring. In all, Abdullah competed in about 10 big matches for JCW.

Chris Hero.t: Chris Hero was featured on JCW Volume 2 as a nobody in what J & Shaggy then called a "Who The Fuck Are These Guys Match" vs Izzy High. Hero then triumphantly returned to JCW's Bloodymania years later as an Indy superstar and one half of The World's Greatest Tag Team along with Claudio Castagnoli when they captured the JCW Tag Team belts after defeating three other teams.

Corporal Robinson.t: "Corp" has a wild story in JCW indeed. This Deathmatch wrestler is somehow undeniably the most successful JCW wrestler in history. He held the World Title for just over 4 years without a single loss. Today he's despised by Juggalos everywhere after he was caught ruthlessly scheming and scamming fans. These antics have left him fired and banned by the company for life. We'll just leave it at that.

DJ Clay.t:
Official DJ for the Insane Clown Posse, DJ Clay is also the House DJ for every JCW event, cranking the theme music for the JCW Roster.

Get to a show early and get hyped as Clay fills the arena with sick jams.

Evil Dead.t: Evil Dead was the first ever JCW World Champion after eliminating the Rock & Roll Express. He went on to perhaps be the most popular wrestler in JCW's history. Current JCW stars The Outbreak are admittedly heavily influenced by the great Evil Dead. A proud but dead member of the JCW Hall of Fame, Evil Dead will never be forgotten.

Forty Winks.t:
We've heard of wrestlers sleeping through their matches before, but nobody does that as literal as Forty Winks. Always prepared for when the Z's strike, Forty Winks wrestles in pajamas with his blanket and pillow close by.

Just be sure not to sleep on him, or you might find yourself looking up at the lights.

Freya the Slaya.t:
The only female wrestler to come out of Alaska, probably because everyone else was scared to get in the ring with her.

"The Arctic Amazon" originally came in to JCW as the muscle for "Broke Ass" Breyer Wellington, who was attempting to use her for his own financial gain. That partnership didn't last long, as Breyer's attempt to punish Freya ended up with him on his back.

Now free from "Broke Ass", Freya is bringing her raw destructive power to the JCW Women's Division with Championship aspirations, as The Queen of The North attempts to become The Queen of JCW.

George Ross.t:
Most referees spend their careers trying to keep wrestlers from getting too violent. George Ross has built his reputation by stepping directly into the middle of the chaos.

Coming from Pittsburgh, George travels the country as one of the most respected officials in professional wrestling. From JCW's insanity to the brutal world of deathmatch wrestling, he has stood between some of the toughest competitors and made sure the rules still matter when things get out of control.

His résumé includes officiating matches for the TNA, NWA, and GCW world championships, proving that whether the spotlight is on championships or complete carnage, George Ross is trusted to be the man in charge. Of course, anyone who has spent time around George knows he isn't exactly a quiet presence. With a booming Pittsburgh voice and a habit of calling everyone "Bubby," George makes sure his instructions are heard loud and clear.

In JCW, where chaos is guaranteed and order is optional, having George Ross in the ring might be the closest thing anyone has to a referee who can handle it all.

Human Tornado.t: This man was a JCW Tag Team Champion along with Zach Gowen as the Pimp & Gimp Connection. A true JCW fan favorite, he recently made a comeback on JCW Lunacy along with Zach Gowen as Violent J's hand-picked opponents for Caleb Konley in J's "4 Weeks of Hell" Challenge.

Insane Clown Posse.t: Violent J and Shaggy 2 Dope founded JCW and won the first Tag Team Championship on night one, defeating two Doink the Clowns.

J-Rod.t:
“The Ultimate Athlete”. An American Gladiator. J-Rod is one of the most impressive athletic specimens in professional wrestling. She made an immediate impact in JCW by becoming the JCW Women's World Champion at Strangle-Mania in Las Vegas after being in the company for less than three months.

Although she possesses a physique and physical gifts that most athletes would be jealous of, J-Rod has no issue taking shortcuts behind the referee's back, earning many victories with the use of brass knuckles. This combined with her arrogance has earned her zero friends in the JCW Locker Room other than her on-again/off-again bestie Sophia Rose.

Attendees of JCW events have reported seeing J-Rod wandering around the crowd insulting every fan she comes in contact with.

Kevin Canady.t: Head trainer of the JCW Wrestling School.

Kid Cadet.t: Kid Cadet is the voice of JCW inside the ring, bringing energy and excitement before every match — and killer outfits to boot — as she introduces all of the talent in JCW.

King Kong Bundy.t: Appeared on the first JCW card, December 19, 1999.

Krule.t:
Not much is known about this masked monster. Rumors have swirled that Krule will take down anyone in his way, whether they are a wrestler or not.

Originally brought in by JCW Co-Owner Violent J as one of Caleb Konley's opponents in "Four Weeks of Hell", Krule impressed the other Co-Owner Vince Russo who had watched his "Chosen One" battle it out with the 6'8" behemoth.

Now a part of the JCW Roster, "The Atrocity" seems fully entrenched in camp Russo. Will he be satisfied being the additional muscle for Caleb Konley, or does Krule have JCW Championship aspirations of his own?

Mac Davis.t:
“Mad” Mac Davis brings something to backstage interviews that professional wrestling has been sorely lacking for years: personality.

He takes no shit from the wrestlers and asks the hard questions. If there's something fishy going on in JCW, Mac will be on the scene demanding answers.

Necro Butcher.t: Necro is a 3-time JCW Tag Team Champion, when he was getting along with Pondo. But when he was feuding with him, the two had some of the most ruthless death matches in JCW history.

Raven.t: Former JCW World Heavyweight Champion and former JCW Tag Team Champion along with his lackey partner Sexy Slim Goodie, Raven made his impression felt in JCW big time throughout several different runs with the company, always helping the show backstage as well and giving his expert advice and input every time. He was always a fun pleasure to work with in JCW and a true future Hall of Famer.

Sally Boy.t:
Young, arrogant, and easily distracted by women, Sally Boy joined JCW on the orders of The Don of the Luciano Family — his uncle Big Vito. Raised by a single mother (Vito's sister), Sally Boy hasn't had much of a father figure in his life until he started working for his uncle.

Things have not gone smooth for Sally Boy in JCW as he frequently makes mistakes due to losing control of his temper, lets his guard down too easily around women, and has even questioned his Uncle Vito's ability to lead the Family.

Will Sally Boy fall in line, or will he challenge his Uncle Vito's place at the top of the Family?

Scott D’Amore.t: We don't have enough room to say how helpful and what an asset this man has truly been to the company. Whether as a wrestler, a manager, a backstage consultant, producer, even as a writer, Scott D'Amore is a true JCW icon in every sense of the word. Since way back in the very earliest days of JCW right up until the modern days of Lunacy, Scotty D'Amore has been a never-ending friend and backstage help from day one till today.

Scott Hall.t: This man was a true JCW legend, appearing with Kevin Nash and Sean Waltman as the JWO on three separate occasions, while also appearing by himself on many, many more occasions. Scott Hall once held the JCW World Heavyweight Championship — a tried and true Juggalo icon who is missed dearly around the world, and one of the greatest superstars of all time, hands down. It was such an enormous blessing to have Scott Hall with us so solidly within the Juggalo Family.

Sewacide.t:
Both feared and mysterious, Sewacide stalks arena corridors waiting to pounce.

He doesn't waste time talking. Sewacide hits the ring fast, mean, and without much warning, leaving opponents to figure out what went wrong after it's already too late.

From high flying affairs with the likes of Ninja Mack to taking on the brutish force of 2 Tuff Tony, he has shied away from no challenge.

The only thing more unsettling than facing Sewacide is trying to figure out what he will do next. And the answer is usually something nobody saw coming.

Sophia Rose.t:
Sophia infiltrated JCW posing as a Ring Girl to help her long time on-again/off-again best friend J-Rod get one over on Alice Crowley.

Appearing to be sweet on the surface, Sophia has been known to throw a temper tantrum or two when things don't go her way inside the ring.

The Great Muta.t: An absolute wrestling God known all over the world. The Great Muta made three special trips to the United States from Japan just to wrestle in JCW. One time he even brought Violent J a Kimono Robe from Japan that actually fit J's fat ass perfectly. He teamed with his protégé Nasowa on 2 occasions before returning to face him in one-on-one battle at Bloodymania.

The Green Phantom.t:
After weeks of very expensive buildup asking everyone to "Get with The Green", the hero that was coming to save JCW was nothing more than a fart in the breeze, briefly stinking up the place before fizzling out with the wind.

The Green Phantom couldn't win a single match. With his introductory vignettes getting more airtime than his matches, Violent J had no choice but to cut his losses. The Green Phantom was fired for poor performance, ending the JCW career of perhaps the company's biggest financial bust.

However weeks later, to the surprise of everyone, The Purple Phantom debuted in JCW with a very familiar outfit, body type, and voice. Somehow The Green Phantom was able to get back into JCW under a different color mask. New color but same results, as The Purple Phantom also blew his chance at staying on the JCW roster.

Have we seen the last of The Phantom? That probably depends on how many different colors of masks he has.

The Iron Sheik.t: Appeared on the first JCW card — December 19, 1999 at St. Andrew’s Hall, Detroit.

The Ring Rat.t:
Ass big as two beach balls, The Ring Rat has gone from star to star in JCW as she lives up to her name.

Joining JCW originally as a groupie for Caleb Konley before he discarded her, The Ring Rat used Disco Ray until she was done with him, leaving him in the dust at Strangle-Mania and moving on to "The Rock God" Steven Flowe.

She's no lover and she ain't your friend, but she's got the skills to help wrestlers succeed in JCW, albeit with her best interests always in mind.

The Rude Boy.t: The Rude Boy is a legit JCW Hall of Famer and legend. A true to life Day 1'er. He held onto the World Title for almost a year straight at one point before having the belt stripped off him due to no-showing events. Later in his career he surprised many with respectable success outside of JCW. To this day he likes to point out that he was never beaten for the JCW World Title. This may be true, but failure to defend it definitely qualifies as a loss.

Trent Acid.t: What can we say that hasn't already been said about this true Indy Wrestling Icon? A former 2-time JCW Heavyweight Champion, Trent Acid was the Shawn Michaels of the Indy scene. Every match he was in was almost always the best on the card. He left this world way too soon. He's prolly slamming fools and flying off the ropes in Shangri La.

Vampiro.t: The only man to ever defend the JCW World Title on WCW's national TV show Monday Nitro and declare it the only belt that matters in pro wrestling, Vampiro is truly the ultimate hero in JCW. A Hall of Famer who's held the JCW World Title on 3 different occasions. You can't be more of an icon in JCW than Vamp.

Veda Scott.t:
Veda Scott has had a successful career inside the ring, winning multiple Championships and being named Pro Wrestling Illustrated's Rookie of the Year in 2012.

Scott brings veteran experience and expertise to the JCW Commentary Table, keeping everyone focused on the in-ring competition despite being surrounded by constant Lunacy.

Vince Russo.t:
When Violent J was looking for an investor to help take JCW to the next level, former WCW Champion Vince Russo used his LLC to invest in JCW anonymously. His lawyers struck a deal for 51% ownership, and Russo immediately changed the landscape in JCW, relieving Violent J of his Commissioner position and putting the JCW Founder out of power.

Russo gave Violent J a chance to earn not only his leadership role back, but for them to share 50/50 Ownership after the war between Violent J and Big Vito was becoming too much for Russo to deal with. Violent J won the stipulation, which meant Russo no longer held Majority Ownership and they would share voting power between them.

There was something else on Russo's agenda. He had a new "Chosen One" that he was going to help take to the top of JCW, and he did just that by taking Caleb Konley under his wing. It didn't take long for Russo's plans to come to fruition, with Konley winning the JCW Lunacy World Championship due to Russo's interference.

Zac Amico.t:
Born in Tromaville, New Jersey (probably), Zac Amico is proof that sometimes the weirdest people end up exactly where they belong.

A stand-up comedian, filmmaker, podcaster, and lifelong fan of wrestling and ICP, Zac has spent years exploring the stranger corners of entertainment. From the bizarre world of Troma movies alongside legendary madman Lloyd Kaufman to his work behind the microphone on podcasts like Midnight Spookshow and Bi Guys, Zac has built a career around making people laugh, cringe, and question what they just witnessed.

Before bringing his twisted perspective to JCW commentary, Zac was already a familiar face in the wrestling world, working as a manager and "Director" of the Hudson County Horror Show for promotions like Catalyst Wrestling and Pro Wrestling Magic. Because apparently managing wrestlers wasn't chaotic enough, someone eventually handed him a headset.

Now, as a voice of JCW, Zac Amico brings the perfect combination of wrestling knowledge, horror movie insanity, and the kind of observations that probably shouldn't be said out loud — but definitely should be heard.

Zach Gowen.t:
For more than two decades, Zach Gowen has made a career out of proving people wrong.

After losing his leg to childhood cancer at eight years old, Gowen refused to let anybody else decide what he could or couldn't accomplish. Instead, he climbed all the way to the biggest stages in professional wrestling, earning worldwide respect with a combination of heart, grit, and a willingness to take risks that would make most wrestlers think twice.

Anybody still expecting Zach Gowen to be an easy night clearly hasn't been paying attention for the last twenty years. When he's not in the ring, Gowen travels as a motivational speaker for kids, making sure the little homies know to not give up their daydreams.

JCW fans know Gowen as a former tag team champion alongside the Human Tornado, but championships only tell part of the story. Year after year, Gowen keeps showing up, keeps competing, and keeps reminding everyone that underestimating him is usually the first mistake an opponent can make.
